title: Traffic Lifecycle Coordinator with Eligibility Priming and Replayable Rollback
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: We need a unified coordinator that can manage small-to-large rollouts (canary, A/B, shadow) while enabling a deterministic, replayable rollback when a safety gate trips. Motivation: Existing controllers handle traffic split and canary phases but lack a deterministic priming step for cohorts and a compact, replayable rollback ledger. This PR introduces the Traffic Lifecycle Coordinator (TLC): a lightweight state machine that manages eligibility priming, shadow priming, phased promote, telemetry gated holds, and a replayable rollback record for bisect/diagnostics. Changeset summary: - Add TLC service (go) with state transitions: PRIMING -> SHADOW -> CANARY -> GRADUAL -> PROMOTED -> ROLLBACK_REPLAY - Implement eligibility priming: cohorts are pre-registered and warmed in shadow mode with controlled sampling to surface integration regressions before traffic is split - Add a compact rollback ledger: snapshots (metadata-only) of routing and cohort assignments are persisted to etcd and an append-only ledger for deterministic replay during rollback or bisect - Telemetry gating: integration with metrics pipeline to evaluate SLOs (p95 latency, 5xx rate, quality regression delta) and hold or trigger rollback when thresholds cross - Replay harness: debug endpoints to simulate replay of a snapshot in dry-run mode against recorded trace samples - Safety gates: sample-weighted statistical checks, time-windowed holds, minimum-sample thresholds, manual-latch override - Operational APIs: rollforward, hold, abort, snapshot, replay-dryrun, audit-export - Migration: automated conversion for existing rollout objects to TLC schema; backward compatible for simple split-based rollouts Backwards compatibility: TLC can be opted-in per namespace. Existing split/canary resources are untouched unless migrated. Checklist: - [x] Service + controller logic implemented - [x] Unit tests for state machine transitions - [x] Integration tests for priming -> canary -> promote -> rollback path - [x] Telemetry gate simulated in CI smoke tests - [x] Migration tool + docs - [x] E2E smoke on staging with shadow priming A/B scenario Performance considerations: priming step uses sampled shadow traffic with throttled concurrency to avoid resource spikes. Ledger entries are compact (<= 2KB per snapshot) and TTL-ed after 30 days by default. Rollback replay reuses existing offline replay infra to minimize new resource requirements. Risks and mitigations: - Risk: mis-priming leads to false positives. Mitigation: default conservative priming sample (0.5% traffic), and manual override. - Risk: telemetry noise causes unnecessary rollback. Mitigation: dual-window gating and minimum sample counts, and a soft-hold mode that requires either two metric windows or manual confirmation. Notes: Linear tickets referenced above capture the product requirements (ENG-1282 describes priming UX; ENG-1305 captures replay ledger format). This description consolidates the scope and operational playbook for reviewers.

review_conversation: Arjun: Nice design. A few questions: how do we protect against ledger growth in a tenant with continuous small rollbacks?
Maya: Ledger entries are metadata-only and TTL-ed; we've added a compaction job to aggregate old snapshots weekly (see ledger.go).
Liam: The replay dry-run looks useful; can it be used to drive automated bisection?
Maya: Not in this PR — replay exposes hooks and instrumentation. I added a follow-up Linear task to plumb automated bisection (ENG-1350).
Sofia: CI didn't exercise the telemetry dual-window gating; can we add a deterministic unit test?
Maya: Added tlc_gates_integration_test.go to simulate sliding windows. That test is part of this PR and passing in CI.
Arjun: Approving pending a tiny logger cleanup and an additional comment on the migration tool behavior during rollback.
Maya: Addressed both in follow-up commits; added comments and a unit test for migration rollback semantics.
